current_primary_sources.evidence: Rustls remains the mature Rust TLS baseline, but official issue 2498 states the project does not support the ClientHello fingerprinting use case and does not intend to expose it in the near future. Current first-party crypto providers include aws-lc-rs and ring, which require native/build scrutiny outside this packet's authorization.

current_primary_sources.identity: official issue closed not planned; inspected 2026-07-27
current_primary_sources.evidence: Maintainers explicitly state rustls does not support JA3/JA4 fingerprinting and will not expose enough ClientHello data for that use case.
Hyper is a mature low-level HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 building block, not a browser fingerprint implementation.
Current source exposes selected HTTP/2 settings values but serializes a library-defined settings sequence; exact browser HTTP/2 wire parity is not a declared compatibility contract.

Reqwest supplies redirects, proxies, cookies, streaming, HTTP/2, and rustls integration. It does not claim browser TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint parity, and its current default rustls feature selects aws-lc-rs.

Wreq provides fine-grained TLS and HTTP/2 browser emulation, but its official README states HTTPS uses BoringSSL and documents BoringSSL build dependencies. It is rejected by the explicit dependency boundary.

Execute security/resource/cancellation semantics through a public candidate-adapter API and real local TCP protocol server where a socket boundary is required.
Represent every requested capability as satisfied or as a typed blocked capability before execution; never substitute ordinary HTTP success for fingerprint parity.
Emit an aggregate PASS_PURE_RUST_PATH only if every mandatory case is behaviorally proven; otherwise emit FAILED_SPIKE_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_DECISION with exact blockers and no dependency exception.

Reqwest/hyper/rustls as proof of browser compatibility because none declares or exposes complete browser TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprint parity.
Hand-authoring a PASS report or comparing fixture labels because behavioral proof must execute the same public acceptance oracle and a behavior-changing counterfactual.
Creating shipped product transport code because this packet is a non-product Phase 0 prerequisite.

assumptions: Loopback is allowed only behind a test-harness capability internal to the non-shipped corpus runner; ordinary SSRF policy must reject it.
A typed blocked capability is a valid failed-spike observation but never an implemented capability.
A future dependency exception is an Operator decision outside this packet.
non_goals: Claiming browser parity from JA3 strings, generic HTTP success, or structural fixtures.

corpus_contract.pass_threshold: Every mandatory case executes its named semantics and passes the same aggregate oracle; any required blocked capability forces FAILED_SPIKE_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_DECISION.

bounds: stream chunk bytes and outstanding byte credits

fail_closed_rules: Reject every disallowed address when any DNS answer is disallowed.
Bind execution to one address from the validated answer set and reject substitution.
Reject proxy requests requiring address-level SSRF proof when trusted destination evidence is unavailable.
Strip origin-bound credentials and recompute cookies on cross-origin redirect.
Accept body bytes only after byte-credit admission.
Do not reuse a connection after unacknowledged or unsafe cancellation.
Block unsupported fingerprint/wire requirements before network execution.
